accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS ELA RI.4.7 (interpret information presented visually, orally or quantitatively, e.g. charts, graphs, diagrams, time lines, and explain how it contributes to an understanding of the text) and the national curriculum in England Years 3–4 reading (retrieve and record information from non-fiction) and Year 3–4 statistics (interpret bar charts with scales). Timeline dates verified: Bell's telephone patent 1876, the Wright brothers' first powered flight 17 December 1903, Apollo 11 Moon landing 1969 (1903 + 66), World Wide Web made public 1991. Every chart value, sum and comparison in the lab, practice and challenge was recomputed (30 = 6 lines × 5, 40 − 10 = 30, 7 × 6 = 42, 14 < 15 = half of 30).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented errors with graphs in texts: skipping the visual because the words seem complete (WHO sort, prediction 1, challenge q2/q6); counting scale lines as 1s when each is worth 5 (prediction 2, READ q1/q2 decoys 6 and 3, challenge q1, m9); reading the neighbouring bar (READ q1 decoy 25); treating the last or tallest bar as most or as more than half (READ q3 Friday, BOTH zoo 14 of 30, m5); 'how many more' answered by adding (READ q4 decoy 50); assuming the order events are mentioned is the order they happened (prediction 3, timeline q1, p5, challenge q5); and answering in the wrong unit from one source (bags not apples).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagvisinf pairs a written passage with its own visual on one canvas: facts are sorted by whether the words, the chart or both carry them; a bar chart with lines every 5 but labels every 10 is read; a timeline is used against a passage that names events out of order; questions are dragged to the visual (bar chart, timeline, labelled diagram, map) that answers them; and three puzzles need a rule from the words plus numbers from a chart. flagbgraph (697) teaches building bar graphs and flagnfind (397) contents/index features; neither compares a text with its visual. lab_distinct gate under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before being told: a fact like 'reached 18 cm' cannot be sorted as words-only because the passage gives no number; tapping 6 for Tuesday returns 'each line is worth 5, so 6 lines make 30'; tapping the first plane flight as earliest returns 'the words name the plane first, but 1876 is before 1903'; dropping 'When did each king rule?' on the map says a map shows where and the question asks when; choosing 7 apples says 7 is bags and each bag holds 6.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each with a tempting wrong option the task then disproves: 'yes, it shows the same thing' (the sort has three chart-only facts), '6' for a bar on the 6th line of a 5s scale (READ q1 and q2 show 30 and 15), and 'yes, the words said it first' (timeline q1 puts the telephone at 1876 before the 1903 flight). A.reveal names the locked-in pick when each task completes.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, twelve wrong-answer messages naming the slip: each line is worth 5 not 1, 30 is two lines above 20, the words already say the town grew, a graph shows numbers not smells, a map shows where not when, a diagram shows parts not dates, 4 is teams not players, adding instead of multiplying, left is earlier on a timeline, words can mention events out of order, and charts carry facts rather than decoration.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid FK grade 1.9 (family limit 5.0), adult 9.8 (limit 10.0). Kid paragraphs use one concrete example each (the 6th line on a 5s scale shows 30; 6 apples a bag × 7 bags = 42). Canvas passages are under 30 words, chart labels are single words, and feedback lines are one short sentence. The lab file was trimmed under the 20 KB pre-commit limit by shortening feedback wording, not by removing any feedback.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs cover why visuals matter, reading a scale, timelines versus word order and joining both sources; adult text gives RI.4.7 and the England reading and statistics links, the check-title-labels-scale routine, what job each visual does, the named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler and the explanation is under 12% similar to every other lesson, including 697 picture and bar graphs and 397 non-fiction text features.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark for all six steps plus wrong-answer states (fact dropped on 'both', 25 tapped for Tuesday, 1991 tapped as first, map chosen for a how-much question, 'We can't tell' on the zoo puzzle). Moved the puzzle feedback above the three answer cards after it overlapped the last card; timeline event boxes alternate above and below the line so 1876 and 1903 do not collide. Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag and tap has a button under the canvas (each bin with the fact named in its label, every answer value, each timeline event with its year, each visual type, each puzzle answer). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the feedback or the confirmed answer, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, charts sit on a white sheet so bar and label contrast is the same in both themes, warnings switch to #fda4af on dark, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.

sources: Common Core State Standards, ELA Reading: Informational Text RI.4.7 (interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively and explain how it contributes to an understanding of the text)
